content: 1. Diphenhydramine and Trihexyphenidyl: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Diphenhydramine and Trimipramine: These drugs decrease cholinergic transmission and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor for enhanced sedative effects. 3. Diphenhydramine and Triprolidine: Both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Diphenhydramine and Trospium Chloride: Both reduce cholinergic effects, potentially leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Monitor closely. 5. Diphenhydramine and Valerian: Valerian enhances the effects of diphenhydramine through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of central nervous system (CNS) depression. Use caution and monitor. 6. Diphenhydramine and Vecuronium: Both reduce cholinergic transmission. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Diphenhydramine and Xylometazoline: Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while xylometazoline decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. 8. Diphenhydramine and Yohimbine: Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while yohimbine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is recommended. 9. Diphenhydramine and Ziconotide: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 10. Diphenhydramine and Ziprasidone: Both increase sedation. Diphenhydramine also reduces ziprasidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to oral forms. Monitor closely. 11. Diphenhydramine and Zotepine: Both increase sedation. Diphenhydramine reduces zotepine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely. 12. Diphenhydramine and Amphetamine: Diphenhydramine may increase amphetamine levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unclear, so monitor closely. 13. Diphenhydramine and Aripiprazole: Diphenhydramine increases aripiprazole levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 14. Diphenhydramine and Ashwagandha: Ashwagandha enhances the effects of diphenhydramine through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution. 15. Diphenhydramine and Brimonidine: Both increase sedation. Brimonidine enhances diphenhydramine’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing CNS depression. Monitor closely. 16. Diphenhydramine and Chlorpromazine: Both increase sedation. Diphenhydramine reduces chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely. 17. Diphenhydramine and Donepezil: Diphenhydramine increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, while donepezil reduces diphenhydramine’s effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 18. Diphenhydramine and Loratadine: Diphenhydramine increases loratadine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Diphenhydramine and Promethazine: Diphenhydramine increases promethazine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 20. Diphenhydramine and Risperidone: Diphenhydramine increases risperidone levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 21. Diphenhydramine and Sedative Drugs (e.g., benzodiazepines, opioids, barbiturates): Co-administration increases sedation. Use caution and monitor for excessive CNS depression. 22. Diphenhydramine and Anticholinergic Drugs: Concurrent use may lead to additive anticholinergic effects, such as dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention. Monitor closely. 23. Diphenhydramine and CNS Stimulants (e.g., caffeine, amphetamines): Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while stimulants decrease it. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. 24. Diphenhydramine and Botulinum Toxins: Anticholinergic drugs like diphenhydramine may potentiate the effects of botulinum toxins, increasing the risk of excessive neuromuscular weakness. Monitor closely. 25. Diphenhydramine and High-Dose Nettle: Nettle enhances diphenhydramine’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Monitor closely. 26. Diphenhydramine and Calcium/Magnesium/Potassium/Sodium Oxybates: Co-administration may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Avoid or use alternative treatments. 27. Diphenhydramine and CYP2D6 Substrates (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine, carvedilol): Diphenhydramine increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 28. Diphenhydramine and Antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, doxepin): Both drugs increase sedation and reduce cholinergic effects. Monitor closely. 29. Diphenhydramine and Antipsychotics (e.g., clozapine, ziprasidone): Both increase sedation. Diphenhydramine may also reduce the levels of some antipsychotics by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely. 30. Diphenhydramine and Opioids (e.g., codeine, hydrocodone): Co-administration increases sedation. Diphenhydramine may also reduce the metabolism of some opioids, affecting their efficacy. Monitor closely. 31. Diphenhydramine and Muscle Relaxants (e.g., cyclobenzaprine, carisoprodol): Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 32. Diphenhydramine and Antihistamines (e.g., loratadine, cetirizine): Co-administration increases sedation. Monitor closely. 33. Diphenhydramine and Donepezil Transdermal: Both drugs may antagonize each other’s effects. Monitor closely. 34. Diphenhydramine and CNS Depressants (e.g., alcohol, benzodiazepines): Co-administration increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to impaired psychomotor performance. Monitor closely. 35. Diphenhydramine and Anticholinergic Adverse Effects: Additive anticholinergic effects may occur with concurrent use of other anticholinergic drugs, leading to increased risk of side effects such as dry mouth, blurred vision, and constipation. Monitor closely. This summary highlights the potential interactions and risks associated with diphenhydramine when used with various medications. It is essential to monitor patients closely and adjust therapy as needed to minimize adverse effects.
